Dashiell Hammett, The Dain Curse.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/dashiell-hammett/the-dain-curse

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Dashiell Hammett, the author, died 1961.

First publication of the text used: 1928 to 1929 in the serial form (Black Mask magazine, United States), then 1929 as a book (SE colophon: 'was published in 1929 by Dashiell Hammett'). Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dain_Curse) says it was serialized in Black Mask in 1928 and 1929 and gives country United States with Alfred A. Knopf as publisher.

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in 1928 and 1929, before 1931, so the United States rule settles the origin too. A published work of that date enters the United States public domain 95 years after publication, so this work entered it on 1 January 2025.
- Country of origin (United States): the same as the United States paragraph above, because the text was first published in the United States before 1931.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."
